scope: Kayenta Obsession second-edition base/core, standard16-round2–4-player multiplayer with base objective deck; marked expansions, optional variants and alternate modes excluded.
assessment: No material rule error or important omission found within the declared scope after independently checking core flow, quantities, costs, timing, destinations, exceptions, scoring and Base-labelled reference entries.

checked_claims.checked_detail: Standard 2–4-player base multiplayer has four seasons, three ordinary rounds per season and twelve turns per player; courtships have no turns, rotation or ongoing effects.
Random first player; family selection starts to their left; reputation and four base-family bonuses match.
Five starting tiles, five servants, four family cards except Asquith, two starter guests and five objectives; unused starter guests rejoin casual deck.
One valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; unused servants unavailable.
Players plus one double-sided monuments, at most one Estate monument, all activity-to-monument suites retained, initial six distinct eligible tiles and duplicate stacking.
Start 1.1 except Cavendish 1.4, five increments per level, minimum1.1 and standard maximum7.5.
Village Fair3/9, objectives6, Builders’ Holiday11, National Holiday14 and courtships4/8/12/16.
Rotation, event before ongoing effects, activity, gentry, service, favours, buying and cleanup; used service expended, gentry personal discard; last player alone advances round.
All service available, all discarded gentry to hand, event/ongoing effects, choose £200 or refresh, optional buy and advance if last. Hiring when passing is excluded optional/expansion content.
Exact type/count, gender includes family, casual/prestige exclude family; screening reputation fixed before step3, later special-action payments may lower actual level.
PR restricts play, not acquiring or scoring tiles/guests; National Holiday waives PR.
Positive before negative, ordinary invite draw/reveal/to hand, screening rejected cards unseen to bottom, optional dismissal from hand/activity/discard to corresponding deck bottom.
Money loss fully payable using positive favours, VP card or borrowing; minimum reputation ignores further loss and prevents opponents targeting.
Borrow2 increments/£100; Service Help3 increments/one Quarters servant to Available; refresh4 increments once/turn; sufficient reputation required, repeat borrowing/help allowed.
Multiple Market Refresh VP cards and passing refresh coexist with one special-action refresh.
Housekeeper substitutes for unavailable lady’s maid; Brushing Room permits footmen for unavailable valets; underbutler substitutes for base male servants even when available.

Butler’s Room activity with no gentry hires up to two common servants free into Expended; upgraded room may instead recruit one common servant from any opponent-board location; unique servants protected.
Only Butler’s Pantry grants underbutler, immediately Expended; not Butler’s Room or VP hire; ordinary two rotations to Available, with documented refresh alternatives.
One servant can be used directly from Quarters each turn without reputation cost, in addition to available service; expended when used.
All five named family entries, including Young Lady conditional male-prestige bonus and Asquith Dowager both favours, match.
Charles/Elizabeth service, favour and8VP values, no PR, prestige status and Young Lady trigger; Florence/Perkins reputation reductions match. Dismissal immunity belongs only to family.
Ordinary first-use upgrade mandatory, ongoing activities unavailable after conversion; hybrids alternate each use and only face-up category scores.
Monument income only ordinary turns; Barn rewards Estate hosting; Servants’ Hall uses one servant to transfer one reputation with minimum-target protection.

Heritage doubles all favours including negatives; Queen doubles one favour; Lionheart draws prestige from deck without personal service, doubles nonnegative favours and keeps guest in discard; one attendee fixed.
Study initial activity two family/butler then Village Fair-only ongoing reward; Library front objective/back VP card with two/three family and butler.

checked_claims.claim: Base West Terrace and other base tile statements
checked_claims.checked_detail: West Terrace remains activity both sides, three family/butler, prestige invite plus optional1–4 dismissals upgraded; alternate ongoing terrace excluded; South Lawn Estate count and Long Gallery reduction match.
Market-space or Reserve £300 plus printed modifier, £100 floor, no duplicate acquisition by any means.
Slide old tiles, stack duplicates without extra spaces, draw until filled, sort only new draws, send eligible new tiles to open Reserve.
Service after first courtship except Largest Wine Cellar; PR1 after second; all Reserve tiles public/selectable, not just top of stack.
Clear Market only, refill before returning old tiles, no immediate reappearance; Reserve movement then mandatory standard seasonal refresh then theme, anticlockwise first player and round advance.
Builders’ Holiday and Market Purchase use one unchanged Market/Reserve with original applicable prices; finish purchases before sliding/refilling; no refresh between purchases.

Seven ordinary objectives less four discards leaves three; extra objectives add retained count; tile ownership sufficient; discarded objectives/VP cards bottom-deck; VP cards immediate/later own turn/final opportunity.
Reputation, money, Market Purchase/Refresh, objective screen, all-service refresh, prestige invite, hire common servant and immediate returned gentry match.
First three current-theme face-up tile VP including negatives; return Fairchilds first; winner VP/Fairchild, ties each VP/no Fairchild; objective discard each courtship.
All four revealed themes, repeat categories count again; reputation level tie-break ignores position; unresolved tied winners receive VP cards under general tie rule; final special actions/VP use.
Face-up tile VP, hand/discard gentry, retained objectives and VP cards, reputation1/3/6/10/15/21/28, every servant2VP, wealth1VP/£200 floor; Fairchild then level then shared victory.
Named tile sets and6/9/10/11/12/12/12/13/16/17VP values match Base-labelled entries; replacement-deck variants excluded.
Guest/category/common-servant bonuses, servant sets, individual tiles, monuments and wealth match Base-labelled entries, including upgraded suite monuments retaining categories.

7VP objective requires maximum reputation level/Max counter in standard play, independently of wheel position. French publisher p.14 explicitly says niveau de réputation maximum and Max counter; p.7 identifies Max as7. No seasonal flow imported from supplemental source.
checked_claims.source_refs: Compendium p.111; Super Meeple official French base rules pp.7,14

independence_statement: Fresh source audit performed against only the supplied summary snapshot and authorized primary source files. I read the relevant core rules, full FAQ and base family/gentry, improvement, VP and Base-labelled objective entries. I read both corrigendum pages and inspected extracted PDF images where text alone was insufficient, including the standard round-track board. The French localized publisher source was consulted only on pp.7 and14 for the unchanged reputation objective. I did not read questions, answer keys, reader responses, grades, previous audits or other QA files, did not communicate with readers, and did not edit or repair the summary.
